[sql] Use ColumnTime() and BindTime() in payments and DPO stores

sql::Statement has ColumnTime() and BindTime() for base::Time columns
and asks callers to use them instead of converting through int64
microseconds by hand. Two stores still convert by hand:

- PaymentsAutofillTable writes the use_date of server card and IBAN
  metadata with BindTime(), but reads it back in four places with
  base::Time::FromDeltaSinceWindowsEpoch(base::Microseconds(...)).
- DeclarativePerformanceObserverStore reads created_at that way, and
  writes created_at and the expiry cutoff of its cleanup queries with
  ToDeltaSinceWindowsEpoch().InMicroseconds().

Use ColumnTime() and BindTime() instead. The on-disk format is
unchanged: both accessors use the same microseconds since the Windows
epoch as the hand-written conversions.

The offer expiry in PaymentsAutofillTable is stored in milliseconds, so
the accessors don't apply to it and it is left alone.

R=fleimgruber@google.com

[Churned-Users][Clank] Add action buttons and wire closed callback

This CL implements the "Turn on" and "No thanks" action buttons for the
Autofill Payments Churned Users bottom sheet on Android and connects
user actions to the preference lifecycle and strike database via a
unified closed callback.

Key changes:
- Layout: Adds "Turn on" (FilledButton) and "No thanks" (TextButton)
  action buttons to autofill_payments_churned_users_bottom_sheet.xml.
- Resources: Exposes accept and cancel button label strings
  (IDS_AUTOFILL_CHURNED_USERS_BUBBLE_ACCEPT_BUTTON_LABEL and
  IDS_AUTOFILL_CHURNED_USERS_BUBBLE_CANCEL_BUTTON_LABEL) to Android
  Java resources.
- MVC Architecture:
  * Adds button label and click handler keys to Properties.
  * Binds buttons and click listeners in View, ViewBinder, and
    Coordinator.
  * Adds a Delegate interface to Coordinator and Mediator to route
    user interactions.
- JNI & Lifecycle Integration:
  * Hooks user interactions through AutofillPaymentsChurnedUsersBottomSheetBridge
    to native C++.
  * PaymentsChurnedUsersUiDelegateAndroid passes a single closed_callback to the
    bridge, which invokes it with the corresponding PaymentsUiClosedReason:
    - Accept ("Turn on"): Invokes closed_callback with kAccepted (enables kAutofillCreditCardEnabled pref and applies 2 strikes).
    - Cancel ("No thanks"): Invokes closed_callback with kCancelled (applies 2 strikes for a 6-month cooldown).
    - Passive Dismissal (swipe down, tap scrim, back press): Invokes closed_callback with kNotInteracted (applies 1 strike for a 7-day cooldown).
    - Show failure / rejected: Invokes closed_callback with kUnknown (no strikes).
  * Consolidates bottom sheet and message UI state tracking under is_showing_ui_.
- Tests: Adds unit tests in PaymentsChurnedUsersUiDelegateAndroidTest
  and Robolectric tests across BridgeTest, MediatorTest, ModuleTest,
  and ViewTest.

Testing visualization:
- Security bottom sheet with buttons:
https://screenshot-v2.corp.google.com/DC2sRFWfH3MA4f8
- Security mock:
https://screenshot-v2.corp.google.com/26fnuscvth7kg
- Convenience bottomsheet with buttons:
https://screenshot-v2.corp.google.com/7gRP3vAP9X9cUAv
- Convenience mock:
https://screenshot-v2.corp.google.com/2hb18bu4peuv0
- Autofill Payment
turns to "On" after clicking "Turn on" button:
https://screenshot-v2.corp.google.com/7uZJ4jXyGd2fXkT
- Strike count +2
when clicking "No thanks" button:
https://screenshot-v2.corp.google.com/2uldb3ob2o510
- Strike count +1 on
passive dismissal of the bottom sheet:
https://screenshot-v2.corp.google.com/1j5s57scs8rlg

See Patch 5&6 for log testing

Store pending suspend/resume promises in BaseAudioContext's list

The Web Audio API spec. keeps an ordered list of pending promises in
BaseAudioContext, while AudioContext additionally keeps a list of
pending resume promises. The separate resume list lets resume()
resolve all the resume promises on success and reject them on failure,
while close() can reject all pending promises including resume
promises via the BaseAudioContext list.

Compared to this, the spec. stores pending suspend promises only in
BaseAudioContext, allowing suspend() resolve the returned promise
on success and reject it on failure, while close() can reject all
including suspend promises.

To match the spec, every suspend()/resume() resolver is now stored in
a BaseAudioContext vector pending_promise_resolvers_, and AudioContext
holds resume() resolver in pending_resume_resolvers_.

To reject or resolve the exact promise returned from suspend(), added
a resolver parameter to AudioContext::PerformTransitionToSuspended().

To handle multiple concurrent suspend() calls, the boolean flag
pending_transition_to_suspend_ is replaced with a counter field
pending_transition_to_suspend_count_. Each suspend() call increments
it and each PerformTransitionToSuspended() decrements it, allowing
close() to cancel all pending transitions by zeroing the counter.

[ContextualTasks][6/9] Move top toolbar controls to toolbar mojom

As part of the Contextual Tasks toolbar rearchitecture, toolbar-scoped
Mojo methods are being migrated from ContextualTasksPageHandler to
ContextualTasksUIBase. This allows the toolbar WebUI to run
independently while strictly preserving all pre-rearchitecture logic.

and the SetExpandButtonEnabled() Page callback from
contextual_tasks.mojom and ContextualTasksPageHandler to
contextual_tasks_toolbar.mojom and ContextualTasksUIBase, updating
TopToolbarElement to use the toolbar browser proxy.

[Fonts] Implement CSS Fonts 4 directional weight matching on Mac

Before this change, `BetterChoice()` and `BetterChoiceCT()`
matched font weights on macOS by minimizing raw
abs(candidate_weight - desired_weight)` with a tie-breaker
away from 500, and `BetterChoiceCT()` also filtered on
`kCTFontBoldTrait` using a threshold of 600. This diverged
from the CSS Fonts 4 section 5.2 directional weight search
algorithm and suffered from spurious bold traits reported by
CoreText/AppKit on non-bold faces (such as `HiraginoSans-W5`
and `PingFangSC-Light`).

This patch matches the spec by following changes:
1. Adds `BetterWeightMatch()` implementing the CSS Fonts 4
   section 5.2 directional weight search.
2. Skips `kCTFontBoldTrait` during family member weight
   matching when `MacFontWeightFromOS2` is enabled, as
   `BetterWeightMatch()` encodes the spec's weight preference
   directly via numeric weights.
3. Enables the `MacFontWeightFromOS2` runtime feature flag by
   default, combining `OS/2.usWeightClass` lookup with
   directional weight matching.

Note that the `OS/2` table is not used for variable fonts, and
that we may experience similar issues such as
crbug.com/543243014 for variable fonts. We may revisit if
future macOS fonts hit the rare condition.

The other previous regression crbug.com/516316384 should not
occur, as this logic uses `ToCSSFontWeight()` instead of
`AppKitToCSSFontWeight()` (which collapsed sub-400 weights).

[predictors] Remove the remaining expired Navigation.Prefetch histograms

PrefetchManager still recorded three histograms:
Navigation.Prefetch.IsHttps, Navigation.Prefetch.PrefetchJobQueueLength
and Navigation.Prefetch.PrefetchJobQueueingTime. They expired on
2025-04-27, 2023-03-19 and 2023-03-19, so the code that records them is
dead.

Remove the recording code together with the comments that explained it,
and PrefetchJob::creation_time, which was only used for the queueing
time. These were the last histograms in prefetch_manager.cc, so the
histogram includes go away as well. QueueingMetricsRecorded only checked
the two queue histograms and is removed. Also remove the histograms.xml
entries.

This follows crrev.com/c/8461862, which removed the expired *BodySize
histograms from the same file.

[Autofill] Make kFieldTypeToTypeName constexpr

- Previously, `FieldTypeToStringView()` constructed
  `kFieldTypeToTypeName` at runtime using
  `base::NoDestructor<base::flat_map<FieldType, std::string_view>>`.
- Since `kFieldTypeToTypeName` is the inverse of the `constexpr`
  `kTypeNameToFieldType` map and is keyed by the `FieldType` enum,
  construct it at compile time as a `static constexpr
  std::array<std::string_view, MAX_VALID_FIELD_TYPE>`.
- Replace the `flat_map` lookup with direct array indexing after bounds
  and non-empty checks, avoiding heap allocation and runtime binary
  search.
- Remove unused `flat_map.h` and `no_destructor.h` includes.

[MiraclePtr] Enforce raw_ptr in templated containers in chromecast/base/observer.h

This change replaces instances of raw C-style pointers (`T*`) with
`raw_ptr<T>` for elements stored inside templated containers (such as
`std::vector` and `std::array`). This aligns with the broader MiraclePtr
safety initiative to protect against use-after-free vulnerabilities.

This advances MiraclePtr's expansion to containers and preempts an
upcoming clang-plugin update that will strictly ban these un-rewritten
instances.

Bug: b:501142609
Doc: go/miracleptr-in-containers

Enable exit-time destructor warnings for media/webrtc browser tests

Remove the no_exit_time_destructors exemption from
chrome/browser/media/webrtc:browser_tests and fix the offending globals:
- multi_capture_usage_indicator_service_browsertest: the InstalledApp
  globals hold key pairs and bundle IDs, and their keys are random, so
  they can't become by-value getters. Parameters now name apps with a
  TestApp enum, and the fixture creates both apps and resolves them with
  GetApp().
- capture_handle_app_window_browsertest: build the per-process window
  title from the process ID instead of caching a random one in a static.
  Tests in one batch still share it, and parallel batches still differ.
- webrtc_getdisplaymedia_browsertest: use a char16_t array instead of a
  std::u16string global.

[WebUILocationBar] Deflake BrowserFocusTest.FocusTraversal

With the WebUI location bar the test failed 11/15 runs locally.

The race: the browser and the toolbar WebUI exchange state over their
own Mojo pipes (ToolbarUIObserver for browser -> WebUI state pushes,
ToolbarUIService for WebUI -> browser actions), which are not ordered
against the frame IPC the test waits on. Concretely:

- After chrome::FocusLocationBar() the test closes the omnibox popup,
  but the resulting popup_open=false push is coalesced into a posted
  task and sent over the observer pipe, while the Tab key is sent over
  the input pipe. When Tab arrives first, readonly_omnibox.ts still
  thinks the popup is open, swallows the Tab and forwards it to the
  browser, which ignores it because the popup is closed.
- FocusNextElement() resumes on OnFocusChangedInPage (frame IPC), but
  IsViewFocused(VIEW_ID_OMNIBOX) reads OmniboxEditModel::has_focus(),
  which is only updated when OnOmniboxAction(FocusChange) arrives on
  the service pipe.

Add FlushWebUIToolbarPipes() to webui_test_utils. It sends any pending
coalesced state push, round-trips the observer pipe (the WebUI has
applied every push and sent its reactions), then round-trips the
service pipe (the browser has handled those reactions). After it
returns, both sides agree on everything that has happened so far. The
test calls it after focusing the omnibox, after closing the popup and
after every Tab.

Test-only hooks added for this: WebUIToolbarWebView::
FlushPendingToolbarStateForTesting(), ToolbarUIService /
WebUIToolbarUI observer flushes, and BrowserProxy.
flushToolbarUiHandlerForTesting() on the TS side so WebUI tests can use
the same flush.

No production behavior is changed.

CONV=a2fc7b0f-acad-418a-ba07-b10f18b41ef6

usb: Invalidate active configuration in UsbDeviceHandle upon ResetDevice

When a USB device undergoes a bus reset, the hardware returns to the
unconfigured state (configuration 0). Previously, UsbDeviceHandle did
not update the active configuration on UsbDevice or clear its claimed
interfaces upon reset. On a multi-configuration device, this allowed
subsequent interface operations to validate against stale configuration
metadata and potentially bypass protected interface blocklists.

This CL updates UsbDeviceHandleUsbfs (Linux, ChromeOS, Android) and
UsbDeviceHandleImpl (macOS) to clear claimed interfaces, refresh
endpoint mappings, and set the active configuration to 0 upon
ResetDevice completion (even if reset fails, as the physical hardware
may have already returned to an unconfigured state), matching the
pattern used by SetConfiguration.

UsbDeviceHandleWin (Windows) is not modified because ResetDevice is
unsupported under WinUSB and unconditionally fails; thus, device
configuration and claimed interface state never diverge on Windows.

[contextual-tasks] Add CopySearchJourneyTabFeature

Add CopySearchJourneyTabFeature and register it in tabs::TabFeatures when
IsCopyTextJourneysEnabled() is true so per-tab clipboard copies, search
navigations, and tab lifecycle events are forwarded to
CopySearchJourneyTracker:
- OnTextCopiedToClipboard captures the source tab's SessionID and last
  committed NavigationEntry::GetUniqueID() and forwards the copied text
  to CopySearchJourneyTracker::OnCopyRecorded.
- DidFinishNavigation checks for committed primary-main-frame non-error
  navigations to Google search URLs matching the default search provider,
  extracts the committed query via
  TemplateURL::ExtractSearchTermsFromURL, and forwards it to
  CopySearchJourneyTracker::OnSearchNavigationCommitted.
- Tab destruction and WebContents discard callbacks invoke
  CopySearchJourneyTracker::OnTabDestroyed to evict stale per-tab state.

Enable ServiceWorkerBackgroundUpdate features by default

This CL enables the features tested in the ServiceWorkerBackgroundUpdate
field trial by default:
- PrewarmServiceWorkerRegistrationForDSE
- ServiceWorkerBackgroundUpdateForFindRegistrationForClientUrl
- ServiceWorkerBackgroundUpdateForServiceWorkerScopeCache
and disables:
- ServiceWorkerMergeFindRegistrationForClientUrl

The field trial has been evaluated on Android and Desktop Stable,
showing statistically significant latency improvements without regressions.

Ref: ServiceWorkerBackgroundUpdate.gcl
Ref: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1h7pBpyQ6KTIy9XwPajy89r7-suiOl-1AhHIaQ4k6Yhg/edit?resourcekey=0-vRSNtG44B7QF4Q9W9wmVyQ&tab=t.0#heading=h.pss9cyvuk8yp

render processes associated with profiles that disable keyed services by

Don't handle extension URL overrides if extensions are disabled

HandleChromeURLOverride and HandleChromeURLOverrideReverse now check if
extensions are disabled for the given profile before processing URL
overrides.

This is a preparatory change for TopChromeWebUIProfile, a new non-user
profile that only hosts Top Chrome WebUI. Extensions are disabled for
it, but it doesn't register the extension prefs, so without this check
these handlers would hit the "Trying to access an unregistered pref"
CHECK. For the System profile, this is a no-op, since extensions can't
be installed there.

[TabModel] Remove obsolete rootId plumbing

Tab groups are identified by Token (tabGroupId) and rootId is
deprecated:
* Remove unused createTabStatesAndMetadataFile overloads, saveTabState,
  writeFile, and createThumbnailBitmapAndWriteToFile from
  HomeSurfaceTestUtils, folding metadata creation into
  prepareTabStateMetadataFile.
* Remove rootId assignment from ColdBackgroundTab and
  LiveBackgroundTab.transferPlaceholderMetadata, as
  TabCollectionTabModelImpl.addTab resets a tab's rootId to its own ID.
* Remove rootId copying from CustomTabResumeManager.cloneTabState, as
  Custom Tabs do not support tab groups.
* Remove rootId resets from TabArchiverImpl.prepareTabState and
  ensureArchivedTabsHaveCorrectFields, as
  TabCollectionTabModelImpl.addTab already resets rootId to the tab's
  own ID when creating or restoring archived tabs.
* Remove unused rootId test state and locals from TabUmaTest and
  TabSwitcherLayoutTest, and update stale rootId Javadocs in
  TabWindowManager, TabObserver, and Tab.

[🌺] Revert "[Tab UI] Convert TabUiTestHelper#enterTabSwitcher() to hop on Public Transit"

This reverts commit a17f49c0a20027255d94c38bc707bb5f7d3a8815.

Reason for revert: consistently fails android-desktop-x64-rel.

ArchivedTabsDialogCoordinatorTest#testMessageResizedOnTablet has failed
in 4/25 recent builds of android-desktop-x64-rel, every attempt in every
one of them. This is not flake: it reproduces on every run, so it blocks
the CQ for every unrelated CL that touches this suite. The regression
appears at refs/heads/main@{#1711641}.

Example failing run:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/try/android-desktop-x64-rel/786883

Converting TabUiTestHelper.enterTabSwitcher() from direct UI-thread performClick() to Public Transit CtaPageStation.openRegularTabSwitcher() (Espresso click) exposes a tablet/desktop orientation relayout race in ArchivedTabsDialogCoordinatorTest#testMessageResizedOnTablet (ArchivedTabsDialogCoordinatorTest.java:845-848), where rotateActivityToOrientation(ORIENTATION_PORTRAIT) immediately precedes enterTabSwitcher() (the same race fixed for testIphMessageResizedOnTablet in https://crrev.com/c/8432406).

Reverting to green the tree first. Please re-land once the failure is
understood and covered; this revert is about restoring CQ throughput,
not about the merit of the change.

Original change's description:
> [Tab UI] Convert TabUiTestHelper#enterTabSwitcher() to hop on Public Transit
>
> First conversion of a legacy test util with TrafficControl#hopOnAt().
>
> enterTabSwitcher(), used by 31 test files, now hops on at the current
> page (a CtaPageStation) and travels to the TabSwitcherStation by
> clicking CtaPageStation#tabSwitcherButtonElement, via the existing
> openRegularTabSwitcher()/openIncognitoTabSwitcher(). This replaces
> performClick() on a raw findViewById() plus a layout wait, and resolves
> the crbug.com/40155797 TODO to click the button through Espresso. The
> util now returns the TabSwitcherStation. Public Transit callers can
> continue from that Station; the others ignore it. Hopping on over a live
> Station in the same Activity logs a warning pointing the caller at
> CtaPageStation#openRegularTabSwitcher() instead.
>
> Also adds TrafficControl#hopOnAt(Activity, Station), the shorthand for
> the common case of hopping on without any action, i.e.
> Triggers.noopTo().hopOnTo(), the counterpart of hopOffPublicTransit(),
> and uses it in HopOnOffUnitTest.
>
> tab_ui:test_support_javalib gains direct deps on public_transit_java and
> chrome_java_transit, whose types TabUiTestHelper now uses.
>
> The waitForLayout(BROWSING) after addBlankTabs() in TabGridDialogTest is
> removed: addBlankTabs() already waits for the BROWSING layout, and the
> duplicate wait was dead code.
>

Enable exit-time destructor warnings for //device/bluetooth

Remove the no_exit_time_destructors exemption from //device/bluetooth
and fix the function-local statics it was hiding:

- Floss GetDBusTypeInfo() specializations keep returning a reference to
  a compute-once static, now wrapped in base::NoDestructor.
- Floss StructReader parse tables, used on every D-Bus message, are
  wrapped in base::NoDestructor.
- FakeFlossAdapterClient's address lookup maps are wrapped in
  base::NoDestructor.
- The macOS LE device watcher builds its plist base::FilePath from a
  constexpr string at each use.

Make chrome://bookmarks/?id= URLs use the numeric IDs

Some user workflows rely on the numeric ids matching up with other
Chrome systems (like extensions or the persisted JSON files). This
requires them to be able to link some sort of IDs together across
systems.

The numeric IDs also come with its own pitfalls, namely that they're not
stable across machines. But since this behaviour is already out in the
wild, we're stuck support it (Hyrum's law....).

[contextual_tasks] Make handler subscribe to tab state

* Add extension handler as tab subscriber to the central tab state
  in contextual search session handle
* Create a push tab state to extension function that is called when
  the tab state is updated via callback. De-duplicate restored tabs
  but not attached tabs, and combine them into a list before
  sending to frontend.
* Do not reset tab state upon handler creation/task id change, as
  session handle should do that. Handler creation happens too often
  throughout session, and tabs would be unexpectedly cleared when
  iframe is added if this were done.
* Add mojo method to send tab updates to frontend subscribers

Enable NavigationNetworkResponseQueue by default on ChromeOS

This is the follow up CL for https://crrev.com/c/8255769.

This CL enables kNavigationNetworkResponseQueue and companion feature
kBeforeUnloadBrowserResponseQueue by default on ChromeOS, making them
enabled by default across all platforms.

Background: In October 2023 (commit edce850a78fff / crrev.com/c/4923816
under crbug.com/281094330), kNavigationNetworkResponseQueue and
kBeforeUnloadBrowserResponseQueue launched on Windows, Mac, Linux, and
Android. ChromeOS was excluded with a TODO due to a trybot issue at that
time.

Also updates WebAppInteractiveUiTest.TabOpensOnCorrectDisplayMultiScreen
to load an installed PWA from embedded_https_test_server() instead of
http://example.org/, avoiding immediate net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED
failures and adding nullptr assertions for app_browser.

WebNN: add ORT session config test switch

Add a testing-only command-line switch that accepts one or more ONNX
Runtime session configuration key/value pairs. Propagate the switch to
the WebNN GPU and compiler processes and apply the entries after each
session's defaults.

Existing entries are rejected so dispatch hardening and execution
provider defaults cannot be replaced. Malformed, conflicting, and
ORT-rejected entries fail fast with diagnostics identifying the input
that failed.

Add hardware-independent coverage for parsing, applying multiple
entries, empty values, conflicts, and ORT errors.

Test: WebNNOrtSessionOptionsTest.* (9 tests)
Test: services_unittests --gtest_filter=*WebNN*

Original change's description:
> Checked Span: Add offset checking tests
>
> When tightened bounds checking is enabled (and the smuggled size is
> available to Checked Span), the Checked Span cannot be constructed any

34a0464556d025859c3206a2422055d359efcc13 [ diff ] 
Reset client cert dialog limit on successful selection

CertificateDialogPolicy limits each WebContents to 5 client certificate
dialogs, to stop a page from repeatedly prompting a user who keeps
dismissing them. The count was only reset on user/browser-initiated
navigations, so successful selections also counted towards the limit.

Every distinct host needs its own selection. On Android, a page that
legitimately needs client certificates for more than 5 hosts (e.g.
Cider, which reaches several *.corp hosts followed by an SSH relay host
via redirect) has all later requests silently dropped with
ERR_SSL_CLIENT_AUTH_CERT_NEEDED, with no UI and no logging. Opening the
page in a second tab appears to fix it since that tab starts with a
fresh count.

Reset the count when the user successfully selects a certificate.
Declined selections still count, so the protection against repeated
prompting is preserved. Also log a warning when requests are dropped
because the limit was reached.

media: Align video frame context menu checks with Desktop

On Android, Item.DOWNLOAD_VIDEO_FRAME ('Download video frame' / 'Save
video frame as...') was gated on mParams.canSaveMedia() and
UrlUtilities.isDownloadableScheme(mParams.getSrcUrl()), which are the
checks for saving the underlying video file (Item.SAVE_VIDEO).

Because MediaSource (MSE) streams like YouTube set canSaveMedia() to
false, 'Save video frame as...' was missing from the video context menu
even though saving a video frame encodes the current decoded frame into
a PNG blob rather than downloading srcUrl.

We now align Android's video frame context menu items (COPY_VIDEO_FRAME
and DOWNLOAD_VIDEO_FRAME) with Desktop's
RenderViewContextMenu::IsVideoFrameItemEnabled() by checking
!mParams.isEncrypted() && mParams.hasReadableVideoFrame() and removing
the canSaveMedia() and isDownloadableScheme(getSrcUrl()) checks from
DOWNLOAD_VIDEO_FRAME.

[pgo] Remove the unused --weight plumbing from merge_steps.py

The only caller that ever passed --weight was process_pgo_data() in the
pgo recipe module, which hardcoded a 5x weight for mac-arm-pgo's
speedometer3 profdata. Desktop PGO profiles are now produced by
//tools/pgo:generate_profile, which applies that weight itself via
llvm-profdata's --weighted-input, and https://crrev.com/c/8425950 drops
the recipe-side hardcode. code_coverage has never passed weights.

This must land after https://crrev.com/c/8425950: until that CL is in,
mac-arm-pgo still passes --weight to this script, and argparse would
reject the unknown flag.

7dabe68d829ea65875c323b7f8bbe798f0dd9b59 [ diff ] 
Blobs: make blob render-initiated registration async (usually)

For BlobRegistry::Register, registration becomes async. For
FileBackedBlobFactory::RegisterBlob, registration remains async (except
when it's not), but UUID generation moves to the browser process, a la
a73219eb4cb139df9b7e79ef8507d3078a97b27e.

The main hiccup is that UUID might be needed by the renderer, and code
currently assumes that's available synchronously. There are 4 main
categories:

1. Debug code (e.g. DVLOG), which isn't that important

2. Serialization (i.e. SerializedBlob), where we can skip/defer getting
the UUID and leave it up to the other side to get the UUID if needed

3. Some internal extensions APIs, see `BlobNativeHandler`

4. DevTools/CDP (see crbug.com/564832094)

For the cases where it's OK if the UUID is missing, introduce and use
`BlobDataHandle::MaybeUuid()`. For this method, the UUID will be
available if the registration has asynchronously returned already, or if
the BlobDataHandle was created with a known UUID (such as from
deserialization).

For the cases where the UUID is truly needed, introduce and use
`GetUuidMayBlock()`, which may have to call
`mojom::Blob::GetInternalUuid()`, which is made synchronous by this
change. (Note that existing callers of this function, which are only in
the browser process, are unaffected because there is still an async
variant generated by mojo's C++ bindings generator.)

UMA has been added to see how often UUID is needed synchronously.

While we're updating the mojom, remove `content_disposition` which is
always empty. See crbug.com/567626023 for follow-up.

Siso v1.6.3 added missing_deps to StepConfig and merges legacy
bad_deps entries into it. Chromium now uses Siso v1.6.4, and both
versions read missing_deps, so reverting the v1.6.4 roll keeps the
allowlist working.

entries are unchanged.

[Extensions] Respect runtime host permissions in ScriptInjectionTracker

ScriptInjectionTracker::DoesScriptMatch() previously checked URL pattern
matching for static manifest content scripts without checking whether
host access was withheld (e.g. "On click" site access) or blocked by
policy/user settings. Additionally, DoesScriptMatch() returned true
early whenever the tab had activeTab for the frame's origin
(HasTabPermissionsForSecurityOrigin()), skipping policy host
restrictions. Since activeTab can be granted on a policy-blocked host,
this marked the process even though no script could inject there.

This CL updates DoesScriptMatch() to:
1. Check PermissionsData::GetContentScriptAccessForSecurityOrigin() for
   static content scripts, matching scriptable_hosts and tab-specific
   permissions at security-origin granularity while respecting withheld
   permissions and policy/user host blocks.
2. Check PermissionsData::GetPageAccess() for dynamic scripts instead of
   the separate HasTabPermissionsForSecurityOrigin() early return +
   HasHostPermission() check, ensuring both static and dynamic scripts
   enforce policy restrictions and still match against
   `script.url_patterns()`.

Since the tracker now respects policy and user host restrictions, this
CL also notifies it when those restrictions change (per-extension
policy, default policy, and user restricted sites), so that unblocking
a host doesn't cause false negatives for already-committed documents.

Don't retry ORB-blocked media range requests

An ORB block is deterministic for a given request, so retrying it in
ResourceMultiBufferDataProvider::DidFail() can never succeed. Fail
immediately instead.

Adds a regression test at a non-zero position (where transient
failures are normally retried) and a contrasting test confirming that
transient errors still retry.

Fix linking in remove circular includes skill.

Because static_libraries, unlike shared libraries, link only the
sources, and not the dependencies, the correct refactor for a static
library differs.

A static library instead requires the sources to be extracted into a
static library, and then the main target is just a group.

Part of LSC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LuFqCJwtzZHuLfoj9yuupZnlCqwnbDXBgmF70tCwxDE/edit?tab=t.0

Generate constexpr file type tables for C++

file_types_data generated a global flat_map and flat_set of std::string,
both with exit-time destructors. Generate sorted constexpr arrays of
string_view instead, with GetMimeTypeForExtension(),
GetDocumentMimeTypes() and IsDocumentMimeType() lookups, and update the

both tables stay sorted for binary search.

Pass payment metadata in Glic experimental triggering invocation payload

Adds an optional payment_metadata bytes field to TriggerActuationRequest
in the experimental triggering proto and plumbs it through the internal
TriggerActuationRequest struct.

Defines a new ExperimentalTriggeringPayload mojom struct and adds it to
the InvocationPayload union, so the browser forwards the metadata
verbatim to the Glic web client as an ArrayBuffer when triggering
actuation. The payload is always attached for trigger requests, even
when the metadata is empty.

Also updates the Glic TypeScript API and host conversions, the
glic-internals invoke options debug string, and adds converter and
coordinator unit tests.

Extensions: Adopt safe JNI pointers for ExtensionActionPopupContents

This is a pure refactoring with no behavior change unless a native
pointer is used after destruction.

ExtensionActionPopupContents takes ownership of its native popup host
from a @CalledByNative constructor via a raw long field, bypassing
compile-time and runtime lifetime checks. Pass the native object as a
JniUniquePtr instead so Java ownership and destruction are enforced by
the type system.

Because JniUniquePtr cannot adopt a raw `this` pointer from inside a
constructor, a static Create() factory constructs the C++ instance with
jni_zero::MakeUnique, moves ownership into the Java peer, and then
attaches to the host once the Java peer reference is initialized. Also
narrow ExtensionActionPopupContents.Natives from public to
package-private.

Ttc: Enabling journaling of server-side events

This CL plumbs the JournalEvents from the server to the SessionJournal
in ttc/core. The JournalEvents are copied into a core/ type
ServerJournalEvent in order to avoid plumbing the proto dependency deep
into core (this matches all other proto events which are translated at
the TtcMesClient layer).

This CL does just the basic plumbing for instant events. Further
functionality and improvements will come as followup CLs.

[Toolbar] Let bookmark bar receive touches during tab sharing

While a tab is captured, TabSharingToolbarContainer is added to
control_container below the bookmark bar. control_container then
covers the bookmark bar and is hit-tested first. No child claims an
ACTION_DOWN in that region, so ToolbarControlContainer.onTouchEvent
consumes it and bookmark bar taps do nothing. Only the tablet find
toolbar was exempt (crrev.com/c/8308413).

Replace the find toolbar check with getBelowToolbarTouchArea(). It
classifies a touch below toolbar_container as on a visible child that
extends below it, in the gap outside those children, or neither.
onInterceptTouchEvent skips swipe handling and touch observers for the
first two cases, as it already did for the find toolbar. onTouchEvent
lets only gap touches through. With no child below toolbar_container,
behavior is unchanged.

Taps on the tablet find toolbar's background are now consumed instead
of reaching the views under it.

ash: Use consistent name "trusted-pinned" for pinned state

"Locked fullscreen" is a Chrome-level browser feature name (e.g. for
locked quizzes and OnTask), which can be confusing when used in window
management where the underlying window state is a pinned window variant
that cannot be unpinned by the user ("trusted pinned").

This CL replaces the legacy "locked fullscreen" naming with
"trusted pinned" across ash, chromeos UI types, exo, and chrome
(WindowStateType, WindowPinType, WM_EVENT_TRUSTED_PIN, WindowState,
and WindowStateDelegate).

Linux: Ensure toolkit text and omnibox chip contrast

Follow-ups to the GTK/Qt light/dark palette mismatch fixes:

1. Omnibox location icon chip: with a system (GTK/Qt) theme, the
   omnibox mixer sets kColorOmniboxIconBackground to kColorToolbar,
   which comes from the toolkit palette, while the chip text uses
   kColorOmniboxText. When the toolkit palette disagrees with the
   browser color mode (e.g. dark Qt palette while the portal reports
   light), the "Chromium" chip text became unreadable (e.g. #1F1F1F
   on #2D2D2D). AddNativeChromeColorMixer now keeps the chip
   background only if it is readable against the omnibox text, and
   otherwise falls back to a subtle tint of the text over the location
   bar background. The chip foreground is likewise kept only when
   readable against the resulting background.

2. Toolkit contrast guard: GTK and Qt themes may provide foreground
   colors that have poor contrast with their own window background
   (e.g. a Qt palette whose disabled WindowText is #ffffff on a light
   window). kColorPrimaryForeground and kColorSecondaryForeground are
   now passed through BlendForMinContrast against
   kColorPrimaryBackground at the readable contrast ratio, and
   kColorDisabledForeground at the minimum visible contrast ratio.

Verified with screenshots under Xvfb + Mutter with both toolkits, and
with new NativeChromeColorMixerLinuxChipTest unit tests, which fail
without the fix.

Related: crrev.com/c/8516637, crrev.com/c/8516717

Tab group visual data and SQLite tab state persistence have fully
migrated to Token-keyed group IDs:

  dead rootId parameter from StorageLoadedData.createTabState.

parent
0855e751a9fbd70f901ed129482b965f41a62339 [ diff ] 
printing: Remove g_browser_process from CreatePpdProvider

CreatePpdProvider reached for the global browser process to obtain the
URL loader factory its PPD fetchers need. Take the factory as a
parameter instead, so the function no longer depends on global state.

The factory is plumbed in from the three call sites:

- CupsPrintersManager::Create gains a SharedURLLoaderFactory parameter,
  supplied by CupsPrintersManagerFactory and by autotest_private.
- LocalPrinterImpl now stores the factory, injected by
  ChromeBrowserMainPartsAsh::PreProfileInit, which passes the same
  factory to AshWebUIConfigManager a few lines below.
- CupsPrintersHandler receives it through the OS settings hierarchy,
  from OsSettingsManagerFactory down through OsSettingsManager,
  OsSettingsSections, DeviceSection and PrintingSection. Those classes
  already thread local_state, application_locale_storage and
  browser_policy_connector_ash the same way, so the factory simply
  joins that group.

g_browser_process is now read only at the two KeyedService factories and
at the browser main parts, which are the established boundaries for
global state.

New parameters are ordered service dependencies first, contextual data
second, and their non-null and lifetime requirements are documented on
the declarations.

TAG=agy

parent
1a63a47443f7cb9f713efd1502ad50998d4dbe5c [ diff ] 
printing: Inject SharedURLLoaderFactory into PPD fetchers

PrinterConfigCache and RemotePpdFetcher took a repeating callback that
dispensed a raw network::mojom::URLLoaderFactory pointer. That
indirection existed to avoid caching a raw pointer, which a network
service restart would invalidate.

A scoped_refptr<network::SharedURLLoaderFactory> offers the same
guarantee with less machinery: URLLoaderFactoryForSystem re-resolves its
backing pipe on every CreateLoaderAndStart(), so holding the reference
across fetches is safe. Replace the dispenser with an injected
SharedURLLoaderFactory and enforce non-null at construction, which turns
a latent null dereference into an early failure.

Two behavior differences follow from this. The factory is now resolved
when the fetcher is constructed rather than on its first fetch, which is
safe at all current construction sites. Requests issued after
SystemNetworkContextManager has shut down are now dropped and reported
as a fetch failure, rather than dereferencing a null pointer.

This also lets printer_config_cache_unittest.cc drop an unsafe
reinterpret_cast and hand over its TestURLLoaderFactory through
GetSafeWeakWrapper() instead.

While here, remove the dead PpdProvider::LoaderFactoryGetter alias.

ppd_provider_factory.cc still reads g_browser_process; a follow-up CL
injects the factory there and cleans it up.

[SidePanel] Close side panel on Deregister() on Android (4/5)

Close the side panel when the showing entry is deregistered on Android.
-SidePanelRegistry::Deregister() closes the side panel (without
 animations) if the entry being deregistered is showing. This was
 disabled on Android until SidePanelCoordinatorAndroid existed
 (crbug.com/489780669).
-Without it, the side panel coordinator on Android isn't notified when
 the showing entry is destroyed. If the side panel is closing with an
 animation at that time, FinishClosingPanel() later crashes with
 "SidePanelEntry is expected to exist."
-Enable this logic on Android. Together with the change to finish an
 in-flight close on a synchronous Close(), the side panel is closed
 while the entry still exists.

[MChips] Support the optional button on large form factors.

When the optional button is shown in the composeplate row, the layout
now depends on the form factor:
- Phones:
  - The optional and incognito buttons are icon-only and wrap content;
  - The composeplate button takes the rest of the row.
- Large form factors (LFF):
  - all three buttons show their text and share the row's width equally.

To support this:
- Add an optional_button_text TextView to the optional button. The
  OPTIONAL_BUTTON_CONTENT_DESCRIPTION property is replaced by
  OPTIONAL_BUTTON_TEXT, which sets the visible text, the content
  description and the tooltip.
- Add an IS_LFF property, set once when the ComposeplateCoordinator
  is created (NewTabPageCoordinator now passes in isLff).
- Add an IS_INCOGNITO_BUTTON_TEXT_VISIBLE property, so that the
  coordinator controls the incognito text through the model instead
  of the view deciding it.
- Add a 12dp composeplate_view_optional_button_margin for sw600dp.

Screenshots: http://shortn/_UK4fPphmnu.

[SidePanel] Settle side panel animations when its tab closes (3/5)

Settle side panel animations when the tab owning the current entry
closes.
-If a tab-scoped SidePanelEntry is showing and the side panel is
 opening/closing with an animation when its tab is closed, the tab and
 its SidePanelRegistry (which owns the entry) can be destroyed before
 the animation ends.
-The state updates at the end of the animation (e.g.
 FinishClosingPanel()) would then crash with "SidePanelEntry is
 expected to exist."
-Now, SidePanelCoordinatorAndroid::OnTabClosed() completes pending UI
 changes while the tab is still alive. Active entries are left as is, so
 undoing the tab closure still restores the side panel.

Replace CompletePendingContentReplacementForTab() with
CompletePendingUiChangesForTab().
-The new helper completes all pending UI changes if either the
 animating current entry or the pending replaced entry belongs to the
 tab. This covers both the new case above and the existing pending
 content replacement case.
-OnTabReparented() also uses it, so an in-flight animation of the
 reparented tab's entry is settled before its cached Views are cleared.

[WebUI NTP on AL] ntp_tiles: Clean up direct pref access in OmniboxEverywhere and CustomizeChrome

Add stateless, read-only static helpers to ntp_tiles::MostVisitedSites
so code outside //components/ntp_tiles can query and observe custom
links / enterprise shortcuts state without referencing raw pref names
and without instantiating the stateful CustomLinksManager or
EnterpriseShortcutsManager (which have pref-writing side effects):
- HasEnterpriseShortcuts(const PrefService&)
- AddEnterpriseShortcutsObserver(PrefChangeRegistrar&, callback)
- AddCustomLinksObserver(PrefChangeRegistrar&, CustomLinksScope,
  callback)

HasEnterpriseShortcuts() is backed by a new static
EnterpriseShortcutsStore::HasPolicyLinks(), which reuses the store's
existing parsing/validation logic.

Use these helpers in OmniboxEverywhereUIManager,
OmniboxEverywherePrefs and CustomizeChromePageHandler, and drop
//components/ntp_tiles:pref_names from the production GN targets in
omnibox_everywhere and customize_chrome.

The enterprise helpers return false / are no-ops on platforms where
enterprise shortcuts are not supported, so the Android-specific guards
in CustomizeChromePageHandler are no longer needed.

Behavior change: enterprise shortcut availability is now determined
from validated, parsed policy links rather than the raw pref list
length, so malformed policy entries no longer count as present
shortcuts.

[SidePanel] Finish in-flight close when Close() is called (2/5)

Finish an in-flight close synchronously when Close() is called.
-Previously, SidePanelCoordinatorAndroid::Close() returned early if the
 side panel was already closing, even when the caller needed the panel
 to be closed synchronously, e.g. because the current SidePanelEntry is
 about to be destroyed.
-The closing animation would then end after the entry was destroyed,
 and FinishClosingPanel() would crash with "SidePanelEntry is expected
 to exist."
-Now, Close() always completes pending UI changes first, which finishes
 an in-flight close while the entry still exists, keeping the hide
 reason from the original Close() request.

[SidePanel] Allow ending animations for a non-current Profile (1/5)

Allow SidePanelNativeBridgeSelector#endAnimations to be called for a
non-current Profile.
-Previously, it asserted that the given Profile is the current Profile.
-Follow-up CLs settle pending UI changes in more places, e.g. in
 SidePanelCoordinatorAndroid::Close() even if the side panel is already
 closed, and in SidePanelCoordinatorAndroid::Destroy(). These can run
 for a non-current Profile, e.g. when closing all incognito tabs from
 the regular TabModel.
-Ending animations doesn't start a new UI change. It only settles the
 ongoing ones, whose callbacks are sent to the native bridge for the
 current Profile.
-Now, the assertion is removed for endAnimations, so native objects for
 any Profile can settle the UI before changing state or being destroyed.
 The Profile parameter, which was only used for the assertion, is
 removed from the Java methods and the JNI call.

settings: Fallback to /privacy after completing /clearBrowsingData

- Deleting browsing data can scrub navigation entries from
  pre-existing tabs, causing the chain chrome://settings -> /privacy
  -> /clearBrowsingData to be broken since /privacy is missing.

- The system realizes this and loads the chrome://settings as a
  fallback.

- This CL changes the fallback to be explicitly /privacy, which is
  aligned with the previous UX.

- Note: This hardcodes /privacy as the fallback, but this fragment can
  appear outside of the standard chrome://settings -> /privacy ->
  /clearBrowsingData route. e.g., chrome://history ->
  "Delete browsing data" -> fires an intent to /clearBrowsingData. This
  case will still fallback to /privacy after a data deletion event.

parent
92dc3f1b8f861d7f23062a4c8952f336f675e272 [ diff ] 
Keep following links when clicking controls inside them

Before CleanUpActivationBehavior [1], activation behavior ran from
default event handlers (via DOMActivate). Those handlers bubble from
the target up the event path until one of them marks the click as
handled. For example, clicking `<a href><button>...</button></a>` ran
the button's default handler, which did nothing, and then the
anchor's default handler, which followed the link. Clicking the same
button when it submits or resets a form, or clicking a checkbox or
radio button, marks the click as handled, so the link is not
followed. Popover and command buttons do not mark the click as
handled, so both the popover/command and the link run. Gecko and
WebKit behave the same way for the simple button-in-link case.

CleanUpActivationBehavior moved activation behavior into
EventDispatcher, following the DOM Standard [2]: the activation
target is chosen before dispatch, and only its activation behavior
runs. Every <button> and <input> has activation behavior per the HTML
Standard [3][4], so a control inside a link always became the
activation target and the link was never followed. That broke
content.

The HTML Standard is likely to change to match what browsers do:

See https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10032#issuecomment-5879250134

This CL restores the legacy behavior under CleanUpActivationBehavior.
After the activation target's activation behavior runs, the
dispatcher walks the rest of the event path in bubbling order,
interleaved with the default event handlers. For each node after the
activation target that has activation behavior, it runs that
behavior, until the click is canceled or marked as handled. Whether a
node has activation behavior is checked at that point, after event
listeners have run, as the default event handlers did. This means
changes made during dispatch (e.g. changing a button's type, adding
commandfor/command or popovertarget, or giving the anchor an href)
have the same effect as before. Interleaving with the default event
handlers lets ancestors such as <label>, whose click handling is in
its default event handler, handle the click before an enclosing link
is followed.

Tests:
- New html/semantics/forms/the-button-element/
  controls-inside-link-activation.tentative.html covers <button> and
  <input> inside a link, for form submission and reset, popovertarget,
  commandfor/command, image, checkbox, radio, and controls without
  activation behavior. Each behavior is tested when present before
  the click, added during the click, and removed during the click.
  It also covers the link gaining or losing href during the click,
  and a canceled click. It passes with CleanUpActivationBehavior
  enabled and disabled. This test is tentative because it doesn't
  match the spec, but it does match browser behavior.
- dom/events/Event-dispatch-single-activation-behavior.html gets a
  baseline with 7 failing subtests (e.g. <a><label><button
  type=button>, where the link is followed). These assert the current
  spec.

See also: https://crrev.com/c/8278919/comment/37da8d8b_d452e3da/

[1] https://crrev.com/c/8278919
[2] https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-dispatch
[3] https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-button-element:activation-behaviour
[4] https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#the-input-element:activation-behaviour

7425a2cf3966b0e09358d1bd7cd7bb20711e02d9 [ diff ] 
Don't exit fullscreen when the browser window isn't presented

The exclusive access bubble's presentation watchdog exits fullscreen if
the bubble isn't successfully presented within 1.5s of being shown.
However, Wayland compositors may legitimately withhold presentation
from windows that aren't visible to the user. For example, niri doesn't
present a window in an inactive tab of a tabbed column, and discards its
presentation feedback. In that case the watchdog always fires, and
fullscreening such a window reverts after 1.5s.

When the browser window isn't presented, the fullscreen contents aren't
on screen either, so there is nothing for the watchdog to protect
against. Only arm the watchdog once the browser window has successfully
presented a frame. If the browser window is presented but the bubble
isn't, the watchdog still exits fullscreen 1.5s later.

Verified in a nested niri session: fullscreening a Chrome window on a
hidden tab no longer reverts, and Chrome remains fullscreen with the
bubble once the tab is shown.

R=japhet@chromium.org

[fuchsia][starview] Use blank 16GB userdata partition for Cuttlefish

The prebuilt userdata.img in the Cuttlefish guest package is formatted
with an initial small ext4 capacity (~576MB). When run_cuttlefish.py
extended the file with truncate, the raw file expanded but the ext4
filesystem metadata remained unchanged without resize2fs. On first boot,
Android mounted the existing filesystem as-is, leaving /data with
insufficient storage to install large test packages (such as the 635 MB
components_unittests-debug.apk).

This CL replaces the prebuilt userdata.img with a blank, zero-filled
16GB sparse image created by partition_creator.create_zero_image().
Because userdata has the formattable flag in Android's fstab, Android
fs_mgr detects the unformatted partition on first boot and automatically
formats the full 16GB with ext4, providing ample room for test APKs and
runtime dex caches.

[html-in-canvas] Do not cull drawable elements under clips

This patch fixes CullRectUpdater::UpdateRecursively to not mark
a subtree as out of the cull rect when
subtree_should_use_infinite_cull_rect is set. Previously, an empty
overflow clip (such as overflow: hidden with zero size) failed the
CullRect::Intersects check even with an infinite cull rect, causing
nested drawable descendants to be culled instead of ignoring ancestor
clips.

[Tab Capture] Fix flakes and re-enable WebContentsVideoCaptureDeviceBrowserTests

This CL fixes several sources of flakiness in the tab capture browser
tests and re-enables the suite across Mac, Linux, ChromeOS, Android, and
Windows:

1. Runtime software compositing fallback (crbug.com/328310851,
   crbug.com/328419809, crbug.com/328658521):
   Even when running GPU compositing test variants, bots without
   hardware GPUs may fall back to software compositing or SwiftShader at
   runtime, causing the capturer to produce I420 frames instead of NV12.
   We now check whether GPU compositing is actually active at runtime
   before expecting NV12 output or strict hardware color tolerances.

2. Cross-site iframe navigations during color changes
   (crbug.com/329435160, crbug.com/329654821):
   Changing the cross-site iframe color by navigating it to a new URL
   causes RenderDocument to swap the subframe's surface, briefly
   exposing the main frame's white background between frames. Updating
   the iframe's background color in-place via JavaScript avoids the
   surface swap and allows removing the Android RenderDocument
   workaround.

3. Mid-test HiDPI auto-scaling in cross-site tests:
   HiDPI auto-scaling is enabled by default and rescales the 200x150 tab
   to 1.5x after the first frame arrives, which in cross-site tests
   causes the main frame and child frame to resize asynchronously across
   processes. Disabling HiDPI auto-scaling in the test capture
   parameters keeps the source resolution stable throughout the test.

4. Racy startup assertion before the first frame arrives
   (crbug.com/540031290):
   Asserting that the capture stack has not started immediately after
   starting the device races with the Viz thread delivering the first
   frame while the UI message loop is pumped. We instead assert that the
   capture stack has started after waiting for the first frame.

Notify Reading Mode of the active tab's translation state

When the EnableTranslatePdf feature is enabled,
ReadAnythingUntrustedPageHandler now observes the active tab's
ContentTranslateDriver to track page translation state changes.

These updates are sent over Mojo to ReadAnythingAppController and
exposed to the Reading Mode WebUI via chrome.readingMode (including
isContentTranslated, isTranslatePdfEnabled, and an
onTranslationStateChanged callback).

No user-visible behavior change. Follow-up CLs use this state to sync
selections between Reading Mode and translated PDFs at paragraph
granularity. This functionality will be used as part of
http://goto.google.com/chrome-pdf-translation-rm.

[iOS] Allow SigninPromoViewMediator use before mostly displayed

The top-of-feed sign-in promo is only logged as visible once at least
two-thirds of it is on screen, so the user can tap its buttons while the
mediator state is still in its initial state.

Rename `SigninPromoViewState::kHadNoInteraction` to
`SigninPromoViewState::kDisplayedWithNoInteraction` and update
`isUsable` to return `YES` in that state. Also document in
`sendImpressionsTillSigninButtonsHistogram` that no impression is
recorded if the user taps the promo before it is mostly visible, and add
a regression unit test for the top-of-feed promo.

[TabUI] Eliminate non-delegate representative tab lookups

TabModel.getRepresentativeTabAt and TabModel.representativeIndexOf each
reconstruct the full representative tab list across JNI. Eliminate their
remaining non-delegate callers and mark the 4 representative-tab APIs on
TabModel @Deprecated:
- TabSwitcherPane.tryToTriggerRemoteGroupIph: Replace
  indexOfTabCardsOrInvalid and countOfTabCardsOrInvalid with
  getTabGroupIdForIndex(int) to read TabProperties.TAB_GROUP_HEADER_ID
  directly from the card model.
- TabGridDialogMediator.onReset: Read tabs.get(0).getTabGroupId()
  directly since all tabs passed to onReset belong to the same group.
- HubTabSwitcherMetricsRecorder.onTabSelected: Replace the
  representative index comparison and TabModel.isTabInTabGroup check
  with previousTab != tab && tab.getTabGroupId() == null, since an
  ungrouped tab is always a distinct standalone entry.
- TabGroupUtils.getSelectedTabInGroupForTab: Add
  TabGroupUtils.getSelectedOrFirstTabInGroup helper to resolve the
  active tab in the group or fall back to the first tab, avoiding calls
  to TabModel.getRepresentativeTabAt and
  TabModel.getGroupLastShownTabId.
- TabModel: Mark getRepresentativeTabList,
  getIndividualTabAndGroupCount, getRepresentativeTabAt, and
  representativeIndexOf @Deprecated.

[a11y] Add crashtests for stale slots in customizable select options

In a customizable select (appearance: base-select), an option's
accessibility child is the <slot> in its shadow root that renders its
content, unless the option holds just a text node, in which case the
option is a leaf.

When an option changes to only have a text child, it becomes a leaf, but
its <slot>'s AXObject is not removed. A tree update already queued for
the slot then runs with a stale or missing parent:

- Replacing the option's element with text fails the DCHECK "Unowned child should have natural parent". Without DCHECKs, the CHECK "No object should be missing its parent" in CheckTreeIsFinalized() can fail instead, depending on when that check samples the tree.
- Removing the option's only element fails the same DCHECK.
- Hiding the option (display: none) right after replacing its element with text fails DCHECK(!ax_object->IsMissingParent()) (crbug.com/500774799). Without DCHECKs, AXNodeObject::ComputeIsIgnored() dereferences the null parent.

This CL adds a regression web test for each case and the
TestExpectations entries. A fix will land in a follow-up CL.

Fix flaky AttachPinnedTabToNewWindow on Mac

The test AttachPinnedTabToNewWindow previously failed flakily on Mac due
to an asynchronous window activation race condition. The test called
OpenGlicForActiveTab(), which hardcodes activating Glic on the first
browser window (browser1). However, the test had just initiated an
asynchronous activation for browser2. On Mac, this asynchronous
activation completes after the Glic widget opens, stealing focus back
and deactivating the Glic instance, which leads to test expectation
failures.

This CL resolves the issue by adding and calling
ActivateWindow(browser1) to explicitly activate browser1 and wait until
the activation completes before Glic is opened, preventing browser2's
pending activation from stealing focus. Additionally, this CL replaces
uses of browser() with GetBrowser() and uses
CreateAdditionalBrowserWindow() for cross-platform compatibility,
including removing ui_test_utils.

[ContextualTasks] Preserve task on same-doc thread title updates

When a query is submitted with Smart Tab Sharing (STS) active,
the webview initially renders the response using the query as
the provisional title. Once response generation finishes, the
webview pushes a same-document navigation with the
server-generated summary title and thread ID.

Previously, DidFinishNavigation required
current_title == query_value to treat thread ID updates as
in-place updates. When the server pushed a generated summary
title differing from the user's initial query, it was
misclassified as a new thread switch. Consequently, a new
task was created, resetting contextual task state and turning
off Smart Tab Sharing unexpectedly.

Treat a same-document navigation with a changed thread ID as
an in-place update only when it was not initiated by a user
gesture. Script-driven URL rewrites from the AI page (thread
ID resolution, title population) carry no gesture, whereas
selecting a thread from history does, so history selection
still creates a new task and resets STS even when the current
thread has not yet received a title.

[BottomBar] Fix orientation runnable lifecycle and debouncing

mPendingVisibilityUpdate is intended to track whether
mModelTokenChangeRunnable is currently posted in mHandler. Previously,
onModelTokenChange() cleared mPendingVisibilityUpdate = false. When
invoked synchronously (e.g. from native initialization, view attachment,
or mediator updates) while an orientation-triggered runnable was already
queued, it prematurely reset the flag without removing the runnable.
This broke debouncing if another orientation change occurred before the
looper drained (allowing multiple runnables to execute), and caused
destroy() to skip removing the posted callback if it was called while
the runnable was still queued.

* Clear mPendingVisibilityUpdate = false inside
  mModelTokenChangeRunnable rather than onModelTokenChange().
* Unconditionally remove mModelTokenChangeRunnable in
  BottomBarContainerCoordinator#destroy().
* Add unit tests verifying that synchronous calls do not allow the
  runnable to outlive destroy() or break orientation change debouncing.

[BottomBar] Record Glic.IneligibilityReason once per cold start

BottomBarActionEligibility.getCandidateExtraAction() previously recorded
Android.BottomBar.Glic.IneligibilityReason on every invocation without
short-circuiting on sCachedCandidateExtraAction. On cold starts
restoring a non-NTP tab, both
BottomBarMediator.updateExtraActionVisibility() and
BottomBarPromoDialogCoordinator.maybeShowPromoDialog() invoke
getCandidateExtraAction(), emitting the histogram twice per startup.

  BottomBarActionEligibility.recordGlicIneligibilityReasonIfNeeded().
* Invoke recordGlicIneligibilityReasonIfNeeded() once from
  BottomBarMediator.updateExtraActionVisibility() alongside
  recordCandidateDecisionTime() and recordCandidateExtraAction().
* Verify single-emission invariant across
  BottomBarActionEligibilityUnitTest and BottomBarCoordinatorUnitTest.

[Updater] Verify protected pipe owner when the server can't be opened

A medium-integrity client can't OpenProcess the SYSTEM updater, so
IsServerElevated rejected every user-to-system mojo connection. On
ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED over the admin-protected pipe, fall back to checking
that the pipe is owned by SYSTEM or Administrators; its DACL denies
other users new instances, so the owner identifies the server.

Mojo's VerifyServerPrivilege shares the owner check and now applies the
same conditions; its other callers never reach the fallback.

Fix flaky SSLUITest.MixedContentWithSameDocumentNavigation

SSLUITest.MixedContentWithSameDocumentNavigation flakes when a
background DSE prewarm prerender navigation completes while
SameDocumentNavigationObserver is waiting for a same-document
navigation. Because SSLUITestBase::SetUpOnMainThread() maps all hosts to
127.0.0.1 and no server listens on port 443, the prewarm prerender
navigation fails with ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED and commits an error page
in the prerender FrameTree.
SameDocumentNavigationObserver::DidFinishNavigation() does not filter by
IsInPrimaryMainFrame(), so it asserts IsSameDocument() on the
prerender's failed cross-document navigation.

Ignore non-primary-main-frame navigations in
SameDocumentNavigationObserver::DidFinishNavigation() and disable DSE
prewarm in SSLUITestBase via ScopedPrewarmFeatureList.

Example failure -
https://chromium-swarm.appspot.com/task?id=7b1396fe41b85011&o=true&w=true

8f784e14e603361ccbbc40b8f2f79b8b16279d0b [ diff ] 
[Linux] Remove portal online state from NetworkChangeNotifierLinux

Netlink is available in the common sandboxed environments (Flatpak
allows AF_NETLINK unconditionally, and the Chromium snap gets
NETLINK_ROUTE via the network plug and "netlink raw" via unity7), so
the XDG NetworkMonitor portal's online/offline state adds little over
netlink while risking a flaky portal forcing Chrome offline.

Remove PortalOnlineState, SetPortalOnlineState, the
kNetworkChangeNotifierPortalOnlineState feature, the GetAvailable
query, and their tests. Connection type comes solely from netlink
again. Portal-based connection cost (metered/unmetered) detection and
its tests are kept.

[html-in-canvas] Rename "CanvasChild" to "CanvasDrawable"

This patch renames CanvasChildPaintState to CanvasDrawablePaintState
and updates related "CanvasChild" types, methods, variables, and files
(such as CanvasChildPaintRecord -> CanvasDrawablePaintRecord,
EffectPaintPropertyNode::State::CanvasChildState -> CanvasDrawableState,

canvas_child_id -> canvas_drawable_id) to refer to drawable canvas
descendants rather than direct canvas children.

Revert "[Tab UI] Convert TabUiTestHelper#leaveTabSwitcher() to Public Transit"

This reverts commit 5b475f58c5ba0e19b637ca348aed73f4738a4426.

Reason for revert:
LUCI Bisection has identified this change as the cause of a test failure. See the analysis: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/bisection/test-analysis/b/6241023534563328

Sample build with failed test: https://ci.chromium.org/b/8668747472622015809
Affected test(s):
[://chrome/android\:chrome_public_test_apk!junit:org.chromium.chrome.browser.tasks.tab_management:TabGridDialogTest#testTabGroupDialogUi](https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/:%2F%2Fchrome%2Fandroid%5C:chrome_public_test_apk%21junit:org.chromium.chrome.browser.tasks.tab_management:TabGridDialogTest%23testTabGroupDialogUi?q=VHash%3A657f1813ec2d27b4)

If this is a false positive, please report it at http://b.corp.google.com/createIssue?component=1199205&description=Analysis%3A+https%3A%2F%2Fci.chromium.org%2Fui%2Fp%2Fchromium%2Fbisection%2Ftest-analysis%2Fb%2F6241023534563328&format=PLAIN&priority=P3&title=Wrongly+blamed+https%3A%2F%2Fchromium-review.googlesource.com%2Fc%2Fchromium%2Fsrc%2F%2B%2F8503098&type=BUG

Original change's description:
> [Tab UI] Convert TabUiTestHelper#leaveTabSwitcher() to Public Transit
>
> Second conversion of a legacy util with hopOnAt(), after
> enterTabSwitcher() in the parent CL.
>
> leaveTabSwitcher() hops on at the TabSwitcherStation it expects to be
> in, which also verifies the HUB is showing before pressing back, then
> transitions to a CtaPageStation for the previously selected tab, which
> it now returns.
>
> The back press uses the standard ConditionalState#pressBackTo() trigger
> without retry, unlike TabSwitcherStation#leaveHubToPreviousTabViaBack():
> a retried back press that lands on the page finishes the Activity.
>

[Actions] Move the IDC to Action ID map into command_id_to_action_id

Extracts the IDC_* -> Action ID mapping used by CommandActionUpdater
into a standalone `//chrome/browser/ui/actions:command_id_to_action_id`
target exposing chrome::GetCommandIdToActionIdMap() and
chrome::GetActionIdForCommandId().

This lets other code (e.g. the browser accelerator table) resolve
command ids to the same actions BrowserCommandController uses without
depending on CommandActionUpdater. No behavior change.

gfx::HDRMetadata: Remove Mac uses of gfx::HDRMetadata::IsValid

Add a `fallback_to_defaults` parameter to
gfx::GenerateMasteringDisplayColorVolume. When false, return null if the
MDCV metadata is absent or entirely unspecified. Use this in
SetCvPixelBufferHdrMetadata, removing its IsValid check.

In VTVideoEncodeAccelerator, make `encoder_color_space_` and
`encoder_hdr_metadata_` non-optional (using ColorSpace::IsValid and
HDRMetadata:: IsEmpty to indicate not-yet-set), and track only the MDCV
and CLLI metadata (the only parts used to configure the session), rather
than gating on IsValid.

This is towards removing gfx::HDRMetadata::IsValid, since it is poorly
defined and unhelpfully complicated.

Fix lifecycle and null-check issues in recent TabFeatures migrations

Fix several lifecycle and null-dereference issues identified across
recent TabFeatures migrations:

1. Guard RecentlyAudibleHelper::FromWebContents() callers against null
   in MediaEngagementContentsObserver, TabsQueryFunction::MatchTab, and
   AudibleContentsTracker. Under TabFeatures, RecentlyAudibleHelper is
   only present on tab WebContents, whereas MediaEngagementService can
   also observe non-tab WebContents in tests or prerender contexts.
2. Guard CoreTabHelper::FromWebContents() callers against null in
   Browser, BrowserUiController, GetContentRestrictions, and
   ContextMenuNativeDelegateImpl, since unit tests using
   TestTabStripModelDelegate or non-tab WebContents may not instantiate
   TabFeatures.
3. Declare TabAndroid::unowned_user_data_host_ before tab_features_,
   glic_tab_indicator_helper_, and tab_alert_controller_ so that the
   host outlives all ScopedUnownedUserData registrations if ~TabAndroid
   runs while those members are still alive.

7b055cfb5ad3a947adf89c384857314892551d66 [ diff ] 
[Linux] Query XDG portal versions per interface

RequestXdgDesktopPortal() used the version of the FileChooser interface
to decide whether the portal is available, and returned that version to
every caller. FileChooser is implemented by a desktop-specific backend,
so on systems without one, every portal client was disabled, including
clients of interfaces the portal frontend implements itself (e.g.
ProxyResolver, Location, PowerProfileMonitor). Conversely, clients of
other backend-implemented interfaces (e.g. Screenshot, GlobalShortcuts,
Secret) were enabled whenever FileChooser was present, even if their own
backend was missing.

RequestXdgDesktopPortal() now takes the interface name and returns that
interface's version. Setup (systemd scope, service start, registration)
still happens once before any interface is queried, so the app is
registered before the portal is first used. Versions are queried once
per interface and cached, and the cache is cleared when the portal
restarts.

- Update all callers to pass the interface they use.
- The print dialog now checks the Print interface version rather than
  the FileChooser version. Only version 1 is required, since
  "has_selected_pages" is ignored by older versions.
- Drop the separate version query in DynamicLauncherPortal.
- Add SetPortalInterfaceVersionForTesting(). SetPortalStateForTesting()
  with kSuccess still reports version 3 for every interface by default.

[Actor]: Introduce ToolDefinitionBuilder

Actor tools declare their ToolDefinition in each ToolRequest subclass's
static GetToolDefinition(), and ToolSchemaBuilder builds the parameter
schema.

Declaring a tool still means calling the ToolDefinition constructor
with a description and a separately built schema, with nothing
checking that the description was set.

This CL adds ToolDefinitionBuilder, a fluent builder that requires a
tool description in its constructor and configures its parameter schema
via ToolSchemaBuilder or base::DictValue. Build() constructs the
ToolDefinition with the accumulated schema. The model-facing name still
comes from ToolIdToName(), so ToolId stays the single source of truth
for tool names. No ToolRequest subclass uses the builder yet; follow-up
CLs register individual tools.
